- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk aversion or market panic.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 5–10% in the following 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days moving toward historical mean), model often fails to correct; apply “mean reversion bias” by lowering forecast 2–5% in next period.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply “early horizon bias” by subtracting 1–3% from first 5–7 forecast points.  
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from negative to positive (e.g., 0.2 → 0.8), model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 2–4% in next 2–3 periods.
